sections.title: General Info
body: Dominican Casino is a capture card game.
Players use cards from their hand to capture cards from the table.
The goal is to collect scoring cards and reach the winning score.

sections.title: Cards
body: Kings have a capture value of 13.
Queens have a capture value of 12.
Jacks have a capture value of 11.
Number cards use their numerical value.
Aces count as either 1 or 14, depending on the play.
An Ace can capture another Ace, or any group of cards that adds up to 14.
Example: an Ace can capture 8 + 5 + A because 8 + 5 + 1 = 14.

sections.title: Game Rules
body: On your turn, play one card from your hand.
If the card matches a card or stack value on the table, it can capture them.
Cards can also be combined into stacks.
Stacks can only be captured by a card matching the stack value.

sections.title: Scoring
body: Most captured cards gives carta: +3 points.
Most spades gives pi: +1 point.
Each Ace gives +1 point.
The 2♠ gives +1 point.
The 10♦ gives +2 points.
Virao points are added separately.

sections.title: Coins
body: Coins are earned during Casino play and added to your wallet after the match.
A take awards coins when you capture 6 or more cards.
Those coins equal the number of cards in that take.
Special cards pay as soon as you capture them: 10♦ adds 2 coins, 2♠ adds 1, and each Ace adds 1.
Look for the bouncing coin markers on special cards and on big stacks that are ready to pay.
At the end of a round, only viraos add extra coins, equal to the virao points.

sections.title: Endgame Rules
body: At 17 points, the player needs both carta and pi to keep those points.
At 18 or 19 points, only carta and pi can count.
At 20 points, the player must get pi or they score 0 for the round.
